label: Contrasted Heideggerian European "ser" with Indigenous-American "estar"
description: Engaging Heidegger’s ontology, Kusch argued that Western philosophy privileges manipulative being (ser), whereas Andean Indigenous thought dwells inside cosmic uncertainty (estar).
dialecticalTension: Decolonizes fundamental ontology from the Andean altiplano.
historicalContext: América profunda (1962) & Indigenous and Popular Thinking (1970).

label: Shaped Dussel’s early Philosophy of Liberation through popular American ontology
description: Kusch’s turn toward Indigenous and popular Latin American symbolic life deeply influenced the Argentine Philosophy of Liberation movement co-founded by Dussel.
dialecticalTension: Links ontological critique of Eurocentrism to liberation ethics.

label: Foreshadowed Andean ch’ixi philosophy of contradiction and Indigenous estar
description: Kusch’s philosophical fieldwork in Bolivia and northern Argentina informed later Andean decolonial thinkers exploring non-Western epistemic ambivalence.
dialecticalTension: Connects phenomenological fieldwork in the Andes with ch’ixi decoloniality.

citations.author: Walter Mignolo & Silvia Rivera Cusicanqui
citations.work: Indigenous and Popular Thinking in América (Introduction)
